items.headline: Stocks surge Monday: S&P 500 posts its best day since April 8
items.note: The Dow rose 1,104 points (2.2%), the S&P 500 gained 2.35% and the Nasdaq jumped 2.74%. A sharp drop in oil prices and renewed chip buying helped, after a rocky week of worry that data-center buildouts could slow. CNBC didn't give closing levels.

items.headline: Fed's Waller says a December rate hike looks likely, maybe a bigger one
items.note: He backs at least a quarter-point hike on Dec. 8-9 even if October inflation comes in soft, and said a half-point hike should be considered if it runs hot. Markets price better than an 80% chance of a quarter-point hike. Higher rates tend to weigh on growth and tech stocks.

items.headline: October CPI lands this morning at 8:30 a.m. ET
items.note: Economists polled by Dow Jones expect prices up 0.3% on the month and core up 0.2%, a slowdown from September's 0.6% and 0.3%. Annual figures won't be published because of the 2025 government shutdown. Producer prices come Friday.

items.headline: Strong October jobs report keeps the Fed leaning toward hikes
items.note: Payrolls rose 165,000 versus 59,000 expected, and unemployment was 4.1%. The 10-year Treasury yield was 4.876% and the 2-year 4.561% on Monday. A solid labor market is good for job seekers but keeps rates high.

items.headline: Nvidia fell more than 4% after CEO Jensen Huang's email to staff
items.note: Huang told employees he was 'unfaithful' to his wife. Reports say the partner, an executive at Nvidia customer Megaspeed, was assessed by U.S. officials to be a Chinese intelligence asset. Trump said the FBI is investigating, and Nvidia's board is also looking into it. Shares were up about 1.8% premarket Tuesday.

items.headline: TSMC's October sales jump 59.7% from a year ago
items.note: Revenue was NT$586.89 billion (about US$17.88 billion), showing AI chip demand is still very strong. TSMC also expects 2026-2028 capital spending to be significantly higher than the prior three years.

items.headline: Anthropic's IPO still expected mid-November on the Nasdaq
items.note: Investors reportedly see a $1 trillion to $1.5 trillion valuation, below the $2 trillion floated earlier. The amended prospectus lists about $895.4 billion of purchase and lease commitments, mostly for compute. CNBC reported no pricing details yet.

items.headline: SoftBank posts a ~$7 billion quarterly loss tied to AI data-center power equipment
items.note: The loss was 1.12 trillion yen, tied to changed plans for U.S. data-center power equipment. Its OpenAI stake has a fair value of $99.6 billion against $54.6 billion invested. Its shares still closed up 13.9% Tuesday.

learn.explain: The yield curve compares what the government pays to borrow for different lengths of time, such as 2 years versus 10 years. Normally longer loans pay more, so the curve slopes upward. On Monday the 2-year Treasury yielded 4.561% and the 10-year 4.876%, so the 10-year paid about 0.3 percentage points more. When short-term yields rise above long-term ones, the curve is 'inverted', which has often come before recessions. The 2-year tracks where investors expect the Fed to set rates, while the 10-year reflects longer-run growth and inflation expectations.
learn.try: Search for the 10-year minus 2-year Treasury spread on the FRED website (series T10Y2Y) and look at its chart.
